title: When the Cover Wakes
premise: Freya Nakamura, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the unexplained loss of his family aboard Flight 4471 three years ago, is assigned to a routine audit when every digital and paper record of airborne Flight 882 evaporates mid-flight. As he digs, he discovers the erasure was no glitch but a coordinated cover-up spanning three governments — and that his own family's crash was the first test of the same technology. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Vesper who once saved his life under another name, Freya must smuggle the flight's black box data to a tribunal in Reykjavik. In the end he chooses truth over the found family of colleagues who beg him to stop, exposing the conspiracy at the cost of his career and nearly his life, but finally laying row twelve to rest.
about_author: Rafael Galloway is a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. He lives near a small regional airfield, where he claims the sound of takeoffs helps him think.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Three years after losing his wife and daughter on Flight 4471, Freya files yet another appeal against the sealed investigation, only to have it rejected within hours. The beat is grief calcified into procedure; he trusts rules because nothing else held.

chapters.title: Routine Audit
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He's assigned a low-stakes compliance review of Meridian Air's fleet and notices an anomaly: maintenance logs referencing a software package called LULLABY that appears nowhere else. Emotional beat: professional curiosity stirring a man who had gone numb.

chapters.title: Eighty-Eighty-Two
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At 34,000 feet over the Atlantic, Flight 882's records vanish from every database simultaneously — manifests, radar history, even the airline's own booking system. Freya watches it happen live. Beat: cold dread; he has seen systems fail, never forget.

chapters.title: The Plane That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with air traffic controller Ines Okafor, who swears she vectored 882 minutes ago. The plane lands safely but officially never existed; passengers disperse into confusion. Beat: gaslighting at national scale, and Freya realizing someone wants this quiet.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Assassin Vesper's POV, unnamed employer, clean contract: make the auditor a problem. But reviewing Freya's file, Vesper recognizes him from a rescue years ago in Jakarta. Beat: a killer's hesitation, the first crack in loyalty to the mission.

chapters.title: Sealed Files
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He pulls the 4471 file through a friend inside the transport ministry and finds LULLABY referenced in a redacted annex. His family's crash may not have been mechanical failure. Beat: grief reigniting as purpose, dangerous and clarifying.

chapters.title: Old Friends
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He confides in his investigative team — Devi, Marcus, and mentor Halvard Rask — who form a protective circle around him. Beat: warmth of found family, and the first lie Freya tells them about how much evidence he has.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. She traces LULLABY procurement across three defense ministries — American, British, Japanese — all funding the same shell contractor. Beat: vertigo; the conspiracy isn't a rogue actor but a shared instrument of state.

chapters.title: The Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. He tracks down a passenger from vanished Flight 882, a whistleblower mid-extraction, who gives him a physical black box duplicate before disappearing. Beat: hope with a timer attached — the man knows he's being hunted.

chapters.title: Jakarta, Remembered
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback to the flood rescue where Vesper, then a soldier, pulled a young Freya from wreckage. Present-day Vesper stalls the contract, reporting technical difficulties. Beat: identity fracture between the person they were and the weapon they became.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. His credentials are revoked, his apartment tossed, and a leak brands him unstable — the same playbook used on 4471's original investigators. Beat: betrayal by the institution that gave him belonging after his loss.

chapters.title: Halvard's Choice
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Rask is offered reinstatement and honors if he delivers Freya. He refuses, burning his own pension to buy Freya forty-eight hours. Beat: sacrifice; found family proven under pressure.

chapters.title: Runway Lights
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A chase through Hamburg's freight terminal as Vesper closes in — then deliberately misses. Freya doesn't see the face, but recognizes the restraint. Beat: paranoia tangled with inexplicable mercy.

chapters.title: What LULLABY Does
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Decrypted documents reveal LULLABY can erase aircraft from global tracking in real time — tested first on 4471, which carried a defecting engineer. Freya's family were collateral in a demonstration. Beat: rage, the darkest hour of motive.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A government liaison offers him everything: truth acknowledged, 4471 reopened, his family named — if he surrenders the black box. Beat: temptation aimed exactly at the wound; loyalty to the dead versus truth for the living.

chapters.title: Confession at Midnight
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper contacts Freya directly, reveals the rescue, and offers testimony in exchange for protection. Two people bound by a single night of grace must now trust each other completely. Beat: fragile alliance, the book's emotional hinge.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Team
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Pressured by debts and threats, Marcus copies the black box data for the liaison. Devi catches him. Beat: heartbreak inside the found family; forgiveness deferred, not denied.

chapters.title: Reykjavik
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Vesper race to deliver the data to an international aviation tribunal before the treaty signatories vote to bury it at dawn. Beat: relentless momentum, every ally spent or compromised.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Freya/Vesper POV. Ambush at the tribunal steps; Vesper takes a bullet meant for Freya and holds off the extraction team long enough for the data to upload publicly. Beat: loyalty paid in blood; truth escaping containment.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Ines Okafor's POV. From the outside, the world reacts: flight 882 restored to record, hearings announced, three governments scrambling. Beat: catharsis at scale — one controller's testimony mattering again.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Vesper survives, detained but alive; Marcus confesses and is quietly forgiven; the 4471 investigation reopens with names attached. Freya declines reinstatement. Beat: grief transmuted — truth didn't heal him, but it ended the lying.

chapters.title: When the Cover Wakes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. At the memorial wall, Freya reads row twelve aloud for the first time in three years, then walks toward a new case — a smaller wrong, but his to answer. Beat: quiet resolve; belonging rebuilt on truth instead of rules.
